answer: The kernel enforces puzzle verification prior to any agent joins the graph, every vertex must stake a small bond that is slashed on duplicate behavior, and a mirror ledger records all registrations so peers can cross-check for clones. Sybil resistance can come from a proof-of-work gate on identity registration: each new agent must solve a per-epoch puzzle whose difficulty scales with the number of active identities, making mass account creation costly.
